title: Flake: stock_rust_client's reconnecting-stream wait misses its 15s budget under full-workspace load
design:
Observed 2026-11-25 during a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
run. Recorded with the numbers rather than fixed, because the right fix
depends on whether this is only load.

WHAT HAPPENED.

  crates/mimid-agent/tests/stock_rust_client.rs:346
  "a StateChange on the reconnecting stream: Elapsed(())"
  test result: FAILED, finished in 18.97s

The assertion is a tokio::time::timeout(PATIENCE, ...) waiting for an
SseEvent::StateChange on a REOPENED event source, after
`b.post(&chat_b, "one more")`. PATIENCE is 15 seconds
(crates/mimid-agent/tests/common/mod.rs:40).

WHAT I CHECKED, in this order:

  - Re-ran the test alone three times: ok, ok, ok, in 2.58s, 2.80s and
    2.66s. So the whole test takes under three seconds unloaded and the
    one 15-second wait inside it expired under a full-workspace run.
  - Whether my change could have caused it: the work in progress was
    bead mimid-1wgh.129 (a MemberError variant, an AgentError variant,
    Agent::rekey, Store::rekey, a recovery branch in
    vtc_backend::export_media_secret, and documentation). None of it is
    on the event-source, SSE or reconnect path, and none of it runs
    unless a media secret is exported. Not proof, but there is no
    mechanism.
  - Re-ran the full workspace with --no-fail-fast afterwards to confirm
    the suite is otherwise clean.

SO IT IS A TIMING FLAKE UNDER LOAD, roughly a 6x slowdown of one wait on
a machine running many test binaries at once.

WHY NOT JUST RAISE PATIENCE. Because 15 seconds for an event that takes
well under one is already generous, and a budget that fails means
something took 15 seconds, which is worth understanding before it is
hidden. Two things to look at first:

  1. Whether the reopened event source's first StateChange waits on
     something with its own timer (a reconnect backoff, a poll interval)
     that is long relative to PATIENCE. A backoff of a few seconds plus a
     loaded machine would explain a 15-second miss without anything being
     wrong.
  2. Whether this test's fixture is heavy enough to be starved: it runs
     TWO daemons and a server in-process, and the full suite runs many
     such binaries in parallel.

If it turns out to be only contention, the honest fix is a longer
PATIENCE for this one wait with a comment saying why, not a global one.

NOT SEEN BEFORE in this session's several full runs, and not seen again
in the run immediately after, so the rate is low. It will bite CI
eventually.
notes:
2026-11-25: did NOT reproduce in four consecutive full-workspace runs
(cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast), all with
stock_rust_client_chats_through_two_daemons passing. Those runs were on
the same machine on which it failed once at 18.97s against PATIENCE of
15s, and they were not lighter: each was a full rebuild of every test
target after clippy and the rustdoc gate had invalidated the profile.

So the one failure looks load-dependent rather than a defect on the
SSE or reconnect path, and the next person should not go looking for a
bug in that path on the strength of it. What would settle it is a run
under deliberate CPU contention, or the test logging what it was still
waiting for when PATIENCE ran out -- today it says only that it timed
out, which is why one failure told us so little.

Still NOT fixed by raising the timeout. A 15s patience that needs
raising is a thing worth understanding.
